title: Flat projective twists: finite presentation, flatness and base-change identifications
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $n\geq0$, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], where relative projective space is [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. Let $\pi:\mathbf P^n_T\to T$ be the structural morphism and put $f=\pi\circ i$. Suppose $f:Z\to T$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each $d\in\mathbf Z$, the restrictions on affine base opens of $i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_T}(d)$, with twists and module pullback as in [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback], glue canonically to an invertible module $\mathcal F_d$ [def-sc-invertible-module] on $Z$. Then $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]; each $\mathcal F_d$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] and flat over $T$, meaning $(\mathcal F_d)_z$ is a flat $\mathcal O_{T,f(z)}$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] for every $z\in Z$. There are canonical identifications $\mathcal F_d\cong\mathcal F_1^{\otimes d}$ for $d\geq0$ and $\mathcal F_d\cong(\mathcal F_1^\vee)^{\otimes(-d)}$ for $d<0$. For every morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pullback $Z'=Z\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] has its induced closed embedding $i':Z'\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_{T'}$, and the projection $h_Z:Z'\to Z$ satisfies $h_Z^*\mathcal F_d\cong i'^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{T'}}(d)$ for every integer $d$, compatibly with these tensor-power identifications.

source.place: Tag 01MT (lemma-apply-modules), tensor powers and rank-one local bases, applied after affine base restriction; morphisms.tex Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper). Base flatness and arbitrary-base-change compatibility are the transition-function calculation in returned proof step 2.

proof.text: The comparison [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] identifies the relative-Proj projective space in the hypothesis with the base-change projective space over $T$, preserving the structural morphism. Thus $i$ exhibits $f$ as H-projective. Moreover $f$ is quasi-compact by the assumed finite presentation. It is therefore projective in [def-pc-projective-morphism], and [lem-pc-projective-proper] gives properness. No finiteness or Noetherian condition on $T$ is used.

For each affine base open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, use the standard opens $D_+(x_j)$ of $\mathbf P^n_V$ in [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. Their inverse images $W_{V,j}\subset Z$ cover $Z$. By [def-pc-projective-space-twist], the degree-$d$ twist has basis $e_j^{(d)}$ with $e_j^{(d)}=(x_j/x_k)^d e_k^{(d)}$ on intersections. The tensor formula [def-pc-module-pullback] makes its pullback free on $W_{V,j}$ with basis $u_j^{(d)}=1\otimes e_j^{(d)}$: the trivialization is $a\otimes(b e_j^{(d)})\mapsto a\,i^\sharp(b)$ and its inverse sends $a$ to $a\otimes e_j^{(d)}$. Its transitions are $(i^\sharp(x_j/x_k))^d$. The relative-projective-space charts agree under restriction on the base; hence on an affine refinement of two intersecting base opens these are the same transition rules. They satisfy the cocycle identity since $(x_j/x_k)^d(x_k/x_l)^d=(x_j/x_l)^d$. The ratios are units on these intersections, also for negative $d$. Apply the sheaf-gluing clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] to obtain $\mathcal F_d$, and clause (1) to glue the local identifications with the prescribed pullbacks. The same clause glues their inverses and proves uniqueness, so the construction is canonical. These free rank-one charts make $\mathcal F_d$ invertible in [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Tags 01MS (lemma-when-invertible), 01MT (lemma-apply-modules), rank-one charts; sheaves.tex Tags 00AL/00AM and 04TN, gluing sheaves and maps

proof.text: On every $W_{V,j}$ the presentation $0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{W_{V,j}}\xrightarrow{a\mapsto a u_j^{(d)}}\mathcal F_d|_{W_{V,j}}\longrightarrow0$ has one generator and no relations. This is finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. For $z\in W_{V,j}$ the basis gives an $\mathcal O_{T,f(z)}$-linear isomorphism $(\mathcal F_d)_z\cong\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The latter is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,f(z)}$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Under this isomorphism the two maps obtained by tensoring any injection with these modules are conjugate; hence injectivity for one is injectivity for the other. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $(\mathcal F_d)_z$ is flat over the base. This argument works for every integer $d$.

source.place: Definition 01BN, definition-finite-presentation; morphisms.tex Definition 01U3, definition-flat; algebra.tex Definition 00HB, definition-flat

proof.text: For $d\geq0$, on $W_{V,j}$ send $u_j^{(d)}$ to $(u_j^{(1)})^{\otimes d}$, with the zeroth tensor power defined as $\mathcal O_Z$ and $u_j^{(0)}$ sent to $1$. Both sides have transition $(i^\sharp(x_j/x_k))^d$, so these isomorphisms and their inverses glue by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules]. For $d=-m<0$, let $v_j$ be the dual basis of $\mathcal F_1^\vee$ in [def-sc-invertible-module], so $v_j(u_j^{(1)})=1$. If $u_j^{(1)}=r_{jk}u_k^{(1)}$, evaluation gives $v_j=r_{jk}^{-1}v_k$. Consequently $u_j^{(-m)}\mapsto v_j^{\otimes m}$ has identical transition $r_{jk}^{-m}$ on both sides and glues, together with its inverse. The tensor powers here are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; on free rank-one modules multiplication of coefficients identifies each tensor power with the module generated by the indicated pure tensor. Thus these are the asserted canonical power and dual-power identifications.

source.place: Tag 01MT, lemma-apply-modules, multiplication and powers; sheaves.tex Tag 04TN, lemma-glue-maps

proof.text: For arbitrary $h:T'\to T$, apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to the standard polynomial algebra defining $\mathbf P^n_T$. On affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T'$ mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T$, the coefficientwise pullback algebra is $B\otimes_A A[x_0,\ldots,x_n]\cong B[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$, by $b\otimes\sum a_\alpha x^\alpha\mapsto\sum b h^\sharp(a_\alpha)x^\alpha$. Its inverse sends $b x^\alpha$ to $b\otimes x^\alpha$. These maps preserve degree, unit and multiplication and commute with restriction in both affine opens, so they are an identification of $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_{T'}}(\mathcal O_{T'}^{\oplus(n+1)})$ with the coefficientwise pullback $h^*\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_T}(\mathcal O_T^{\oplus(n+1)})$ in the sense of [def-nagata-graded-algebra-pullback-data]. Thus the relative-Proj isomorphism identifies $\mathbf P^n_{T'}$ with $T'\times_T\mathbf P^n_T$ and sends every coordinate ratio to the same coordinate ratio with coefficients in $B$. These affine descriptions cover $T'$ and agree on restrictions. The fibre-product universal property identifies $Z\times_TT'$ with $Z\times_{\mathbf P^n_T}\mathbf P^n_{T'}$. Its projection $i'$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

On the inverse image of $W_{V,j}$ in $Z'$, [def-pc-module-pullback] gives the basis $1\otimes u_j^{(d)}$ of $h_Z^*\mathcal F_d$. The module $i'^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{T'}}(d)$ has the corresponding basis $u_j'{}^{(d)}$ from [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Send $1\otimes u_j^{(d)}$ to $u_j'{}^{(d)}$ linearly. By step 5 the two transition factors are both $h_Z^\sharp(r_{jk})^d$, because ring maps preserve products and inverses of units. Thus these maps and their inverses glue by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] to the required canonical isomorphism for every $d\in\mathbf Z$. To check compatibility with step 4, trivialize on these same opens: for $d\geq0$ either composite sends the pulled-back basis to $(u_j'{}^{(1)})^{\otimes d}$, including $1$ for $d=0$; for $d=-m$ either composite sends it to $(v'_j)^{\otimes m}$, where $v'_j(u_j'{}^{(1)})=1$. The local tensor comparison is $(a\otimes u)\otimes(b\otimes v)\mapsto ab\otimes(u\otimes v)$, and the dual comparison sends the pulled-back dual basis to $v'_j$. These are isomorphisms on the displayed bases. Hence the diagrams agree locally, and the uniqueness clause of the same gluing lemma proves their global commutativity.
